newsitem.title: ITALY: International peace meeting opens in Rome.
newsitem.headline: International peace meeting opens in Rome.

text.p: Cornelio Sammaruga, president of the International Committee of the Red Cross, on Monday urged dignitaries attending an international peace conference to actively campaign for stricter laws on arms trading.

"I should like to ask all of you here...to make a solemn commitment to imposing strict limits on the transfer of arms, not only nuclear and strategic weapons, but also those that are killing and maiming even as we speak...," Sammaruga told politicians, diplomats and business and religious leaders attending the conference's opening session.

He said stricter controls were needed because weapons such as anti-personnel land mines and automatic firearms "circulate freely in the world without arousing any sense of responsibility in the people who manufacture them".
The annual international meeting for religious dialogue is organised by the Roman Catholic community Sant'Egidio.

"We are here to continue on the path of dialogue initiated by Pope John Paul 10 years ago when he gathered leaders of all great religions in Assisi for a common prayer for peace," Andrea Riccardi of the Sant'Egidio community said.

"We have great expectations from these four days of dialogue because the link between a truly religious behaviour and peace is today more evident than ever in the history of humankind," Cardinal Camillo Ruini, chairman of the Italian Bishops' Conference, said.
European Commission president Jacques Santer said a united Europe was a necessity for peace.

"The need to unite the European people in order to cope with the economical challenges as well as the political, social, and cultural ones is more than ever a question of our days," Santer said. "Tolerance is not sufficient for peace. Peace is also a question of permanent dialogue and active will."
Pierre Sane, secretary general of the human rights group Amnesty International, asked religious leaders to support his organization's campaign for refugees to be launched next year.

"We seek to join forces with all religious groups and all religions across the world to usher in an international human rights order. I appeal to you today to join us in our campaign ... Let us remind the world's governments that every single asylum-seeker is a human being," he said.
